paper_level_summary_zh: 该引用论文在相关工作中将[23]作为RFID语音窃听的代表性工作之一，提及其实现了穿墙窃听，但未直接引用其亚毫米级精度或具体方法。

evidences.evidence_quote: Wang et al. [23] extended RFID sensing to enable through-wall eavesdropping.
evidences.evidence_context: Sound is a mechanical wave that travels through vibration. RF signals can detect voice remotely in soundproof environments, overcoming limits of traditional audio sensing. They interact with the environment during propagation-such as via Doppler and multipath effects-to capture sound-induced vibrations. TagMic [22], built with COTS devices, was the first to show RFID tags could be used for eavesdropping. Wang et al. [23] extended RFID sensing to enable through-wall eavesdropping. RF-Mic [20] uses RFID tags to create a low-cost, hidden, and flexible voice monitoring system, marking an early application of RFID in voice surveillance.
